name: Scream
label: Dischord
lede: Two brothers from the Virginia suburbs who put out Dischord's first full-length album by a single band, were one of the first American hardcore bands to tour Europe, and gave a 17-year-old named Dave Grohl his first real gig.

eras.title: Rock and roll in a hardcore town
eras.text: Scream came together in Bailey's Crossroads, Virginia, and found the D.C. punk and new wave scene the way a lot of suburban kids did: through Bad Brains. What set them apart early was a rock and roll streak the city bands didn't have and didn't want.

years.h: The Stahl brothers start a band in Bailey's Crossroads
years.p: [[Pete Stahl|9241a075-b363-477a-88ba-dfa8910b0b13]] sings, his brother [[Franz Stahl|b41d6d0a-bfd7-4927-96cf-7273a320d02a]] plays guitar, [[Skeeter Thompson|f308929f-4345-4c02-b2fe-0871c7762c8b]] plays bass. [[Kent Stax|c1e2187d-d4c7-428f-a4c8-3b4043f31591]] takes over the drums from original drummer Steve Atton not long after the start.
Scream record their debut at Inner Ear with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] and Don Zientara producing alongside the band.

eras.title: The first full-length
eras.text: Dischord had put out singles, a sampler and a split LP when Scream handed it a whole album of their own. They followed it with a heavier record, a second guitarist, and trips overseas that almost no American hardcore band was making yet.

years.p: Seventeen songs, and the first full-length album on Dischord by a single band. The suburbs had beaten the city to the LP.
years.xp:
Up to this point Dischord had released singles, the Flex Your Head sampler and the Faith/Void split. Still Screaming was a different kind of statement: one band, one long-player, with a streak of rock and roll that the straight hardcore bands around them left alone.

Dischord re-cut the LP in March 2009, and it has stayed in print.

years.h: This Side Up, and a second guitar
years.p: For album two, Scream add [[Robert Lee "Harley" Davidson|01bf2142-0999-4077-8a59-11256ff80016]] to thicken the sound in the studio and on stage.

years.h: Over the ocean before almost anybody
years.p: Scream tour hard across the US and then Europe and the UK. Dischord calls them one of the first US hardcore bands to make that trip.

eras.title: The kid on the drums
eras.text: When Kent Stax left, Scream found a teenager from the local scene who fibbed about his age to get the job. Four years later the band came apart on the road and the kid went north to Seattle.

years.p: Stax leaves for personal reasons. Grohl auditions, tells the band he's older than he is so they'll take him on tour, and gets the job. He drops out of high school in his junior year to go.
The third album, and the last with Stax behind the kit.

years.h: Grohl sits in for Iggy Pop in Toronto
years.p: On a Scream tour stop in Toronto, Grohl ends up drumming for [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] at a CD release event.

years.h: No More Censorship, on a reggae label
years.p: Grohl's first studio album with the band, and Scream take it to RAS Records, a reggae label, instead of Dischord.
Scream tour Europe again. A show in Alzey becomes Your Choice Live Series Vol. 10.

years.h: The bass player leaves mid-tour, and the band is done
years.p: [[Skeeter Thompson|f308929f-4345-4c02-b2fe-0871c7762c8b]] quits in the middle of a tour and Scream fall apart on the spot. Pete and Franz stay in North Hollywood and start Wool. Grohl calls a friend for advice.
years.xp:
On an earlier West Coast run, Grohl had become friends with [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]], and Buzz Osborne had brought [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] to see Scream play. With the band suddenly gone, Grohl phoned Osborne, who told him [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] needed a drummer and passed along their number.

Grohl moved to Seattle and joined Nirvana that year.

eras.title: One more record, one more Christmas
eras.text: Scream's last studio album of the original run came out three years after the band stopped, with a Nirvana drummer on it. After that came a string of one-off reunions, including a Christmas show back home.

years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear with Eli Janney producing, and out three years after the breakup. Grohl wrote and sang Gods Look Down.
The Stahls, Thompson and Grohl go back out to support the record.

years.h: A one-off at the Dragonfly, with Zack de la Rocha
years.p: Scream play a single reunion show in Los Angeles, and [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]]'s Zack de la Rocha joins them.

years.cap: The Black Cat, Washington, D.C., December 1996.
years.h: A Christmas reunion at the Black Cat
years.p: Scream come home for a holiday show at the Black Cat in D.C. The night is recorded and released in 1998 as Live at the Black Cat on Torque Records.

eras.title: The original four, and a last goodbye
eras.text: The original line-up came back together and stayed together, with Grohl now hosting them rather than drumming. Their final album became a portrait of D.C. music across six decades, and it arrived weeks after they lost the drummer who'd been there from the start.

years.h: The original line-up, back at the Black Cat
years.p: Stahl, Stahl, Thompson and Stax on one stage again.
An ad hoc Scream line-up helps the club celebrate three decades.
Seven songs recorded live by John Lousteau at [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]'s Studio 606 in Los Angeles, with the original line-up. Their old drummer is now the host.

q: Kent is the original heartbeat of Scream.
years.p: The drummer on Scream's first three albums dies at 61. The band called him irreplaceable, and remembered him as a fisherman, carpenter and train enthusiast as well as a drummer.
years.xp: Stax joined not long after the band formed and played on Still Screaming, This Side Up and Banging the Drum. He came back for the reunions, and played in other bands including The Suspects and the Daryl Davis Band. He was married to his wife Andrea for 40 years.

years.p: The longtime D.C. drummer, who also plays on DC Special, replaces Stax.

Recorded by Don Zientara at Inner Ear shortly before the studio was evicted, with guests from six decades of D.C. music, among them [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]], [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] and Amy Pickering.
years.xp: Scream built the record as a history lesson: the band invited its whole music community in to weave the story of Washington music into the story of Scream. It was also one of the last records Zientara made at Inner Ear, forty years after he helped produce Still Screaming.

sources.title: Stereogum: Scream drummer Kent Stax dead at 61
